metadata.name: Andy Burnham
metadata.description: Labour prime minister advocating stronger public control of essential services, regional devolution and reform of Britain’s relationship with Europe.
metadata.scope: Current documented governing or campaigning position through 4 October 2026. Recent conduct is prioritised; earlier material is used only as a stated continuity-based inference. Party proposals are attributed as the leader’s endorsed programme, not implemented law. Every answer is an interpretive assessment, with lower confidence for biomedical hypotheticals and fine-grained psychological causation. No scores were targeted.

answers.rationale: His proposed electoral reform is explicitly to be submitted through an election manifesto, affirming competitive electoral authority.
His electoral-reform commission is advisory, with the final programme offered to voters; experts do not choose the government.

His conference speech explicitly describes his father failing the eleven-plus examination yet repeatedly exercising his vote, and presents that participation as valuable. This supports qualified education-independent voting rights; the speech does not expressly discuss every possible cognitive qualification, so strong agreement is not inferred.
He proposes bills to Parliament and an election mandate, providing evidence against legislative override by the prime minister.

Independent peer review: Universal vote and equal campaign conditions require a franchise/electoral-rights bridge beyond inclusive reform rhetoric. The actual speech also praises a low-education father voting: a qualified education-independent franchise inference is stronger than the current broad slogan, but exact universality remains qualified.
